# Impact Brief: Toward a persistent event-streaming system for high-performance computing applications

## The Contribution

High-performance computing workflows have long faced a tension between the persistence and fault tolerance of parallel file systems and the speed of direct inter-component communication, with no existing solution adequately addressing both concerns in HPC-specific contexts. This paper introduces Mofka, a persistent event-streaming framework built on the Mochi HPC data service toolkit, designed to bring event-driven, Kafka-style streaming architectures to HPC environments while accommodating their distinctive requirements: massively multicore nodes, RDMA-capable high-performance networks, specialized multi-link network fabrics, and large scientific data payloads. Mofka is evaluated against Kafka and Redpanda on Argonne's Polaris and Oak Ridge's Frontier supercomputers, achieving up to 8× higher throughput in certain scenarios, and is demonstrated in three real-world use cases—tomographic reconstruction, metal-organic framework discovery for carbon capture, and Dask workflow provenance tracking. By providing a modular, lightweight streaming layer that retains data persistence without the API constraints or I/O bottlenecks of parallel file systems, Mofka enables HPC applications to adopt event-driven workflow patterns that were previously impractical at supercomputer scale.
